rationale: The ground truth's sole substantive concern (trust_remote_code incompatible with kernels<0.15.0, no lower bound) was already resolved upstream by commit 9947f414; both candidates correctly identify this and flag the now-stale PR description, giving comparable recall. Y's review is higher signal: it adds a sharp, testable, novel finding (get_kernel with no version/revision raises ValueError on kernels>=0.15, contradicting the docs/pyproject version pins) and ties the sticky-fallback issue directly to the PR's own stated motivation (429 rate limits) with tighter reasoning. X cites exhaustive file:line evidence but buries genuine findings under redundant 'claim-verified' scratch-log entries repeating the same trust_remote_code point three times, plus an irrelevant 'skill candidates' section, which hurts precision and practical usefulness despite similar actionability.
